profile.reading:
Digital West was founded in 1999 in San Luis Obispo and grew over two decades into one of the Central Coast's principal independent providers of fiber connectivity, colocation, cloud hosting and business telephone service. In January 2017 the company acquired Norcast Telecom Networks, which it described at the time as the Central Coast's premier data and telecom provider; the merger combined roughly 60 employees and more than 2,500 business customers under one roof and pushed Digital West's minimum symmetrical fiber offering to 100 Mbps. Digital West operated its primary data center in San Luis Obispo alongside smaller points of presence in New York, Los Angeles, San Jose, and, internationally, Australia and Switzerland, giving Central Coast customers interconnection options beyond the local market.

In January 2021, regional fiber operator Wave Broadband acquired Digital West, adding California's Central Coast to Wave's West Coast fiber network. Digital West's local team, brand, and existing customer relationships were retained rather than folded into Wave's own name; Wave was subsequently absorbed into the Astound Broadband family of brands, and the San Luis Obispo operation is marketed today as Astound Business Solutions, powered by Digital West.

The facility on file here sits at 3620 Sacramento Drive in San Luis Obispo, a multi-tenant commercial building where Digital West shares space with several unrelated businesses, including a local radio broadcaster and a transportation provider, rather than occupying a free-standing, purpose-built data-center structure. That arrangement is typical of regional colocation providers serving a mid-size metro area: technical space is built out inside leased or owned commercial square footage sized to the local market rather than as a standalone campus.

No power capacity, redundancy tier, or square footage figure for the technical space at this address has been published by Digital West, Wave, or Astound at any point across the company's ownership changes, and none could be independently confirmed through public property or business records for this entry. What is documented is a stable, decades-old regional internet provider that grew into a colocation and cloud operator, changed corporate ownership twice, and kept its physical San Luis Obispo location and local brand intact throughout, itself a useful signal of the facility's continuity even without published technical specifications.

reading.body:
The operator of this facility is not published and could not be verified through available research tools. The address and facility name appear in public records, but without a website, operator specifications, or power capacity disclosures, nothing about this campus can be read as material to AI scaling decisions.

California has 103 mapped data center facilities of which 11 publish power capacity figures totaling 365 MW. This facility does not appear among those 11 and publishes no specifications for IT load, cooling, electrical supply, or water availability. Its rank by published megawatts is therefore not applicable.

Without disclosed power capacity, electrical interconnection, cooling infrastructure, or grid access details, this site cannot be evaluated for relevance to AI workload hosting or for its position in the state's data center footprint.
